subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: After the `code_mode_exec` normalization blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept policy-active Codex sessions being routed through unified exec and starting fresh when native hook relay config fingerprints drift?
rationale: That choice changes tool-execution routing and persisted Codex thread continuity for existing policy-active users; code inspection can identify the risk, but only maintainers can decide the intended upgrade/security tradeoff.

options.title: Fix normalization, then review tradeoff
options.body: Repair the Code Mode policy-surface gap first, then have maintainers explicitly accept or reject the unified-exec and fresh-thread behavior before merge.

options.title: Pause until packaged Codex proof
options.body: Keep the draft paused until the bundled `@openai/codex` package version is proven to emit the required native PreToolUse events without a local patch.

options.title: Choose a broader fail-closed path
options.body: If maintainers do not want to rely on positive native hook delivery, close or supersede this PR in favor of an explicit fail-closed or native-surface-disable strategy.

recommendation.title: Fix normalization, then review tradeoff
recommendation.body: Repair the Code Mode policy-surface gap first, then have maintainers explicitly accept or reject the unified-exec and fresh-thread behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the same native hook fallback surface makes this the best available routing candidate for the compatibility/security tradeoff.
